sections.title: Executive Verdict
paragraphs: Pritika Engineering Components is a capital-intensive castings and machining business serving tractor and commercial-vehicle supply chains, principally through its listed parent. It has scaled organically, but the evidence does not yet establish a self-financing compounder. Consolidated revenue grew at 25.28% annually from FY23 to FY26, while the incremental post-tax operating return on gross operating capital was only 4.52%. Customer advances from the parent explain much of the reported operating cash flow. [E04, E07, E08]

This is a cyclical capacity-expansion thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. At the dated ₹80 quotation, the actual post-allotment market capitalization is ₹260.52 crore. Ordinary prospective returns and a buy-price recommendation remain unscored because the March-to-October funding bridge is incomplete. A fully funded hypothetical rescue is costly: the base case requires ₹137.88 crore of net new equity over the modeled period and delivers approximately −1.89% annualized at ₹80. That is a scenario, not a prediction of an actual capital raise or evidence of a historical default. The decisive improvement would be collection-led cash generation and higher capacity returns without further parent-advance dependence. [E14, E15, E24]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
paragraphs: The issuer is Pritika Engineering Components Limited, NSE SME symbol PRITIKA, ISIN INE0MJQ01020, CIN L28999PB2018PLC047462. This is not Pritika Auto Industries Limited. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; the retained exchange price is ₹80 on 19 October 2026. The investment horizon ends exactly 20 October 2031, or 1,826 days divided by 365.25. The nominal pretax equity hurdle is 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities. The illustrative position is ₹500,000, not a statement of the reader’s holdings. [E01, E14, E20]

FY23–FY26 consolidated financials cover PECL and Meeta Castings. Q1 FY27 adds Omnia Engineering Inc., a newly subscribed US subsidiary with nil reported revenue and profit in that quarter. The subscription is an internal group transfer, not a purchase from an outside seller. The model restricts ₹0.47 crore from domestic liquidity without counting it again as acquisition capex. Consolidation does not make parent-company cash or guarantees freely available to PECL minorities. [E18, E28]

G1 is Conditional: the parent is both controlling shareholder and dominant customer, but the inspected records do not prove diversion or minority abuse. G2 is Conditional: FY24–FY26 main and internal-control opinions are unmodified, yet database-level edit logging was not enabled and the first consolidated FY23 cash-flow presentation is unreconciled. G3 is Hold, not Fail: the ₹17.2247 crore parent-loan increase preceding conversion lacks a dated receipt or reclassification bridge; modeled cash deficits also depend on explicit capex, deposit-access and timing assumptions. G4 is Conditional: the lot and actual quote are verified, but 17 scheduled sessions have unresolved missing rows and executable depth is unknown. [E10–E15, E20]

Confidence is High on current audited P&L, recorded allotment terms and the dated price; Medium on organic growth, capital-return economics and the audit interpretation; Low on current cash availability, future financing terms and execution liquidity. The overall investment conclusion therefore has Low confidence even though the arithmetic is reproducible. No absence of daily private bank statements is itself treated as misconduct or a failed funding gate.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
paragraphs: The nine business/growth factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 3, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. The investment factors are R NS, D 3, P 2 and L NS. Each is assigned once and reused with the exact framework weights. BQS is 4.94, displayed 4.9. Raw GQS is 5.90; the persistent weak-capital-return and cash-realization ceiling reduces final GQS to 5.00, displayed 5.0. This is not an extra undisclosed discount. [E04–E10, E13, E19, E24]

IAS is NS. Its supported contribution is 0.25 × 4.94 + 0.20 × 3 + 0.10 × 2 = 2.035. R and L carry 45% missing weight, giving diagnostic bounds of 2.485 to 6.535, or 2.5 to 6.5 displayed. These are missing-factor bounds, not a valuation interval, recommendation, or imputed score. The calculation retains Decimal inputs, full raw precision and ROUND_HALF_UP presentation. Current quotation evidence cannot compensate for an unverified current cash bridge. The company is excluded from an investable IAS ranking while the hold remains.

sections.title: Business Overview
paragraphs: PECL manufactures grey-iron and ductile/SG-iron castings and machined components, including heavier components used in tractors, commercial vehicles and related equipment. Foundry conversion, machining, quality consistency and timely delivery matter more than consumer branding. Customers qualify components and suppliers, but OEM purchasing power remains substantial. Much of PECL’s economic access to end OEMs is intermediated by the parent. This creates recurring order access while concentrating counterparty and minority-governance exposure. [E05, E06, E18]

FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹161.8741 crore, compared with standalone revenue of ₹144.3701 crore. Meeta’s gross subsidiary turnover was ₹31.77 crore, so consolidated revenue does not equal the sum of both standalone revenues: approximately ₹14.266 crore is eliminated. Meeta’s incremental consolidated contribution is about ₹17.504 crore, not the full ₹31.77 crore. Its reported PAT of ₹0.7642 crore included a ₹0.7505 crore tax credit; PBT was only ₹0.0137 crore. Treating that subsidiary as already delivering robust operating profits would be misleading. [E02, E27]

Revenue is recognized on delivery/control transfer under the stated accounting policies; collections can be helped by supplies/tooling advances. Those advances are operating contract funding, not automatically interest-bearing debt. Nevertheless, they are claims on future production and can conceal weak cash realization if their growth is treated as recurring profit conversion. Inventory and GST balances consume capital before final cash reaches the listed entity. [E07, E12]

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
paragraphs: The strongest plausible advantage is a combination of OEM qualification, machining competence and group customer access. Mechanism: a qualified, consistent supplier reduces rejection and switching costs. Evidence: ongoing group/OEM relationships and PECL sales volumes rising from 9,037 tonnes in FY24 to 10,616 tonnes in FY25. Durability: qualification creates friction, but no verified exclusive contract, market-share denominator or consistently high excess return was located. Failure mode: a capable foundry wins a new platform, the parent reallocates orders, or an OEM reprices suppliers. This supports MOAT 5, not a structural-moat claim. [E05, E06, E18]

CARE describes raw-material price adjustments with a lag of roughly a quarter. Therefore, higher sales realization can reflect commodity pass-through rather than stronger pricing power. Metal, power and labor inflation can compress the interval between cost increases and customer repricing. Lost-foam technology and heavier components are management’s differentiation narrative; observed incremental returns remain the more demanding test. [E05, E08, E18]

Other Indian foundry and automotive suppliers can be relevant operating comparisons, but aluminium casting, forging and diversified component groups differ in process, customer mix and asset intensity. No unverified peer multiple is used to justify the valuation. The terminal range of 7x–12x EBITDA is an analyst sensitivity, with 13x in the grid, not a claimed contemporaneous peer median. Independent issuer-level market share and a same-period industry-growth benchmark remain ND. That limits claims of share gain, not the verified absolute revenue expansion.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
paragraphs: The preselected scoring window is FY23–FY26 consolidated revenue, four observations spanning three intervals: ₹82.3230 crore to ₹161.8741 crore, a 25.28% CAGR. The starting REV score is 8. No adjustment is made for the single strong June quarter. The full historical table also retains FY20–FY22 audited standalone observations. A simple FY21–FY26 cross-perimeter CAGR is contextual only because Meeta was not then a comparable operating subsidiary and the pandemic affected the earlier base. A ten-year CAGR is unavailable for an issuer incorporated in 2018. [E02–E05]

Annual consolidated revenue additions were ₹5.0009 crore in FY24, ₹30.0597 crore in FY25 and ₹44.4905 crore in FY26. The Meeta investment was an internally developed capacity addition, not purchased outside revenue. Nevertheless, capacity expansion, internal transfer eliminations and metal pass-through prevent every rupee of consolidated growth from being equated to physical-volume growth. [E02, E04, E27]

A consistent consolidated pass-through cross-check strengthens the selected window: revenue less materials consumed and the inventory-change expense yields pre-conversion-cost value added of ₹30.1431 crore, ₹34.2333 crore, ₹49.4866 crore and ₹67.0818 crore in FY23–FY26, a 30.55% CAGR. This is an analyst proxy before labor, power and other conversion expenses, not statutory gross profit or pure physical volume. It reduces the risk that the nominal 25.28% scoring basis is merely a metal-price illusion; the lower nominal rate is retained, with no bonus for the higher proxy. The same consolidated perimeter is maintained. [E04] The clearest volume/price check is the comparable FY24–FY25 standalone series. Sales volumes grew 17.47%, while standalone sales grew about 20.26%; implied revenue per tonne rose about 2.38%. This supports substantial real volume growth in that period. IPO production volumes were 3,965, 5,252 and 6,619 tonnes in FY20, FY21 and FY22, with installed capacity of 9,600, 12,000 and 12,000 tonnes. Production and sales are different measures, so the old table is not silently used as a sales-realization series. FY26 company-level sales tonnage and a full price/mix bridge were not located. [E05]

Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹52.9305 crore versus ₹37.1745 crore, up 42.38%; PBT rose only 4.51% to ₹2.5359 crore. TTM sales are FY26 plus Q1 FY27 less Q1 FY26, or ₹177.6301 crore. This is a like-period calculation, not four times one seasonal quarter. Omnia contributed nil revenue, so it does not explain the increase. Latest quarterly cash flow is ND. [E19, E28]

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
paragraphs: Growth is accessible through higher utilization, additional machining capability and Meeta’s ramp. CARE reported PECL capacity of 18,000 tonnes annually and FY25 volume of 10,616 tonnes, suggesting headroom, but capacity is not an order book and foundry capacity may not match every machining bottleneck. Tractor demand is cyclical and tied to agricultural income, monsoon conditions, credit and replacement decisions. Railways, defense and overseas diversification are optional development avenues, not recognized base-case sales. [E05, E18, E29]

Capital efficiency is the limiting variable. Normalized operating NOPAT rose from ₹5.6293 crore in FY23 to ₹10.9246 crore in FY26. Gross operating invested capital, before offsetting customer advances, rose from ₹74.6553 crore to ₹191.8909 crore. The ₹5.2953 crore NOPAT addition divided by ₹117.2356 crore added capital is 4.52%. Netting customer advances raises the proxy only to 5.97%, still below the stated 12%–16% nominal post-tax capital-cost range. This is a corporate incremental proxy across a capacity build, not proof of each machine’s project return. [E08]

FY24, FY25 and FY26 gross incremental returns were approximately 1.50%, 11.84% and 2.94%. A ramping plant can depress current returns, and unfinished CWIP may produce future profits. However, the multi-year result, cash-interest burden and cumulative reinvestment prevent assuming that the ramp will automatically create value. CAP 3 and CASH 3 are persistent weaknesses, so the GQS ceiling of 5 is explicitly applied. The base model’s 2.0x incremental sales-to-growth-capex ratio is already a constructive forward assumption relative to the weak observed capital build; 1.25x is stressed. [E08, E09, E23]

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
paragraphs: The parent supplied ₹143.0316 crore of FY26 related-party sales, or 88.36% of consolidated revenue; related-party purchases were ₹14.6123 crore and interest paid to the parent was ₹1.1026 crore. Such concentration is not itself abuse, but minority returns depend on transfer pricing, collections, capital allocation and the parent’s willingness to sustain support. The parent’s post-allotment direct holding is 23,669,016 shares, approximately 72.68% of PECL’s issued equity. A current pledge/encumbrance reconciliation beyond the inspected sources remains ND. [E06, E14]

Actual 17 October allotment matters more than the earlier proposal. Five million shares at ₹64 converted ₹32 crore of parent debt without fresh cash. Another 1.2 million shares brought ₹7.68 crore cash, and 400,000 warrants brought only ₹0.64 crore upfront. The remaining ₹1.92 crore is optional and is not treated as received. Issued shares increased from 26,365,030 to 32,565,030. Using the stale security-master share count would understate market capitalization by ₹49.6 crore at ₹80. Regulatory approval and a debt conversion do not establish that all historical advances were cash received on the conversion date. [E14–E16]

FY26 managerial remuneration of ₹0.5677 crore and remuneration to a KMP relative of ₹0.27 crore total ₹0.8377 crore, approximately 11.46% of PAT. The comparable FY25 amounts were ₹0.4807 crore and ₹0.15 crore. Auditors reported remuneration within the applicable limits. A complete five-year like-for-like remuneration series is not presented as verified. These figures merit monitoring but do not prove excess extraction. [E21]

The prospectus scheduled commercial production for the subsidiary in March 2023; CARE later reported commissioning in April 2024. The scope/phasing of the two statements is not fully reconciled, so this is a delivery question rather than an assertion that every project was late. The FY25 rating described further machining capex targeted for FY26, while FY26 accounts show ₹42.49 crore cash capex and ₹11.94 crore CWIP remaining. Sales growth demonstrates execution, but commissioning and profit milestones need explicit reconciliation. [E29]

The statutory auditor is Sunil Kumar Gupta & Co. The FY26 AGM notice states that its first five-year appointment ends at the ninth AGM and proposes a second two-year term through the 2028 AGM, with annual audit fees not exceeding ₹5 lakh plus taxes and expenses and separately approved permissible services. The notice is a proposal, not treated here as proof of subsequent approval. No resignation citing withheld information was found in the inspected reports. A clean opinion is not used as a substitute for the related-party and audit-log analysis. [E10]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
paragraphs: Full main audit, CARO references, internal-financial-control and audit-trail reporting were inspected, rather than relying only on the directors’ summary. FY24–FY26 opinions and IFC conclusions are unmodified. Auditors did not report borrowing defaults, willful-default status or fraud in the inspected statutory reporting, and bank current-asset returns were stated to agree with books. Yet database-level direct-change audit trails were not enabled for PECL and Meeta across all three years. No tampering was detected where logging operated. This recurring control limitation is not converted into a fraud allegation. [E10]

The GST inverted-duty refund issue is a key audit matter. The company’s input/output tax structure creates recoverable balances, and auditors considered management’s assessment reasonable after their procedures. FY26 balances with government authorities reached ₹9.852 crore versus ₹3.7994 crore. That remains a liquidity and recoverability sensitivity, not an audited qualification. The July 2026 exchange response corrected missing half-year wording in the audit report; it did not announce a restatement of earnings. [E11, E12]

The first consolidated FY23 cash-flow statement begins with PBT of ₹8.6716 crore, versus ₹3.9950 crore in its P&L, and uses zero opening cash. This ₹4.6766 crore discrepancy is not repaired by invention. FY23 CFO and capex are retained as reported but excluded from the comparable cash-conversion period. The FY25 cash-flow comparative was regrouped in FY26, including taxes paid; total CFO changed by only ₹0.0001 crore. Early IPO figures and later FY22 comparative figures are kept as separate vintages. In FY20, the prospectus cash-flow PBT is ₹0.1514 crore versus P&L PBT ₹0.1493 crore, and cash taxes are a ₹0.0190 crore refund. The reported ₹0.9316 crore CFO is retained without inventing a repair. [E03]

For FY24–FY26, reported CFO totals ₹38.3962 crore against PAT of ₹16.4147 crore, apparently 2.34x. However, supplies/tooling advances rose from ₹20.8677 crore at March 2023 to ₹49.3715 crore at March 2026. Neutralizing that ₹28.5038 crore increase and ₹0.6331 crore supplier financing leaves ₹9.2593 crore, or 0.5641x PAT, before cash interest. After ₹15.5247 crore cash interest, conversion is negative ₹6.2654 crore, or −0.3817x PAT. Reported CFO less cash capex and interest is negative ₹75.30 crore over those three years. These are analytical reclassifications, not assertions that accounting CFO was misstated. [E07, E09]

A.Treds supplier financing is reported in other financial liabilities. Suppliers had already received ₹0.6326 crore, with PECL owing ₹0.6331 crore to the financier over 90–120 days. It is added once to debt and removed once from operating payables; its cash-financing benefit is neutralized once. Accrued interest ₹0.2893 crore, capital creditors ₹0.6684 crore, retention ₹0.0957 crore, statutory dues ₹0.5944 crore and leave/gratuity-type provisions ₹0.2284 crore are modeled as legacy payments, not silently lost or double-counted as both working capital and debt. [E07, E13]

FY26 financial reconciliation is explicit: equity plus borrowings and supplier financing, plus excluded financing/tax-like liabilities, less cash, deposits, nonoperating advances and financial/tax assets equals ₹142.5194 crore net operating IC. Adding ₹49.3715 crore customer funding gives gross operating IC of ₹191.8909 crore. The guarantee of ₹12.11 crore for consolidated Meeta debt is not added a second time; the parent’s ₹107.6949 crore guarantee is support, not cash owned by PECL. Letters of credit of ₹1.3008 crore are contingent exposure, not an immediate assumed full cash loss. [E08, E13, E22]

Ageing provides important counterevidence: Note 40 puts all ₹26.6079 crore of March 2026 receivables in the undisputed, considered-good, under-six-month bucket, versus ₹14.6685 crore a year earlier. This does not prove that every invoice is within its contractual due date. Note 41 places ₹2.2052 crore MSME and ₹8.3940 crore other trade payables in the under-one-year bucket, with no disputed category balance; Note 42 places all ₹11.9421 crore CWIP under one year and reports no temporarily suspended project. A granular inventory obsolescence/ageing bridge was not located. Cash weakness is therefore principally the funding and advance bridge, not a claimed demonstrated aged-debtor crisis. FY26 operating EBIT covers interest about 2.37 times; debt plus supplier finance less cash is about 4.57 times EBITDA before giving credit for deposits. These are March ratios, not asserted current October leverage. [E07,E10,E13]

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
paragraphs: Using actual issued shares after 17 October, equity capitalization at ₹80 is ₹260.5202 crore. FY26 reported P/E is approximately 35.64x; TTM PAT of ₹8.2660 crore gives about 31.52x. These are share-count-consistent descriptive ratios, not value conclusions. TTM profit includes a significant quarterly deferred-tax benefit. There is no falsely precise current EV because cash and debt between March and October are not fully reconciled. Simply reducing March debt by the whole ₹32 crore conversion produces an unsupported residual of ₹66.1566 crore; accounting for the missing parent-loan increase gives an illustrative debt-only ₹83.3813 crore before subsequent amortization and supplier finance. [E13–E15, E19]

The principal valuation is mid-cycle EV/EBITDA linked to monthly/event-date cash flow through the exact horizon. Terminal EBITDA applies the margin to the annualized exit revenue run-rate, not to realized trailing-twelve-month sales or EBITDA; this run-rate convention is explicit and somewhat more favorable in a growing business. Bear/base/bull growth is 4%/15%/24%, EBIT margin is 6.5%/9%/11%, and exit multiple is 7x/10x/12x. Depreciation is 4.3% of sales. Maintenance capex is also 4.3%, plus growth investment and a first-year pipeline allowance. Tax is 25% without usable-loss credits, debt interest is 10% in base and 12% in bear, and the current-amortization proxy is ₹12.3739 crore annually until the residual cash-credit balance remains. This is an explicit debt-runoff convention, not a claim that every future contractual installment has been independently verified. [E23]

The March-to-entry operating path is a retrospective hypothetical scenario using a smooth FY26 revenue base and the stated scenario margins. It does not splice in the verified June-quarter revenue or P&L; those figures and TTM comparisons are reported separately. Therefore, modeled pre-entry cash deficits, entry cash and pre-entry rescues are not a reconstruction of actual Q1 operations or bank cash. Hypothetical pre-entry rescue shares are included in scenario entry shares, but are not part of the actual 32,565,030 issued shares at the cutoff. The funding Hold rests on the unresolved material parent-loan/current-liquidity bridge, not proof of a historical default from this counterfactual path. All unrescued scenarios breach a required cash floor, including before entry, so ordinary and conditional nonrescue returns and entry prices are null. An October receipt cannot cure an earlier breach in the model. These deficits are conditional on the selected timing/capex plan, not observed historical defaults. The tests vary accessible deposits from none to all nonpledged deposits, the analyst reserve from ₹1 crore to zero, receipt timing, parent-advance roll-off, and a no-new-parent-cash reclassification. No uncommitted revolving facility is invented. [E15, E23, E24]

Explicit rescues issue whole shares at each interval start, before named investment, working-capital and debt-service uses; gross proceeds, 3% fees and net cash are separately retained. At a fixed hypothetical ₹48 issue price, base net rescue is ₹137.8793 crore and terminal shares reach 62,178,291. Post-entry share expansion of about 76.46% is different from ownership dilution of about 43.33%. Base terminal value is about ₹72.71 per share, giving −1.89% annualized at ₹80; bear is approximately −21.92% and bull 10.37%. Future equity at ₹48 is not committed capital. [E24]

At the base growth and margin assumptions, the funded reverse solve requires approximately 21.7166x terminal EBITDA to reach the 15% hurdle. The growth-only bracket from 0.1% to 120% has no crossing under fixed ₹48 rescue economics, so it is explicitly reported as no valid root. Raising growth cannot automatically overcome capital consumption and dilution. [E25]

Fixed-₹48 rescue entry sensitivities are roughly ₹41.26, ₹36.15 and ₹31.79 at 12%, 15% and 18% hurdles. They are not a buy range: lower entry prices would depend on future investors paying the same relatively high fixed rescue price. A full rerun with rescue priced at 60% of each tested entry yields only about ₹6.04 at a 12% hurdle and no valid funded price root over ₹0.10–₹200 at 15% or 18%. This is why the ordinary entry-price field remains NS. Both growth/multiple and working-capital/capex grids rerun the complete cash path. [E26]

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
paragraphs: The strongest bear case is not simply a lower tractor multiple. Demand slows while inventory and GST refunds absorb cash; parent advances stop growing or run off; debt service and unfinished capex continue; and fresh equity is issued at a discount. The operating business can survive while existing shareholders lose economic ownership. A linked bear case uses 4% growth, 6.5% EBIT margin, longer collection/inventory periods, 50% advance run-off, 12% interest and 7x terminal EBITDA. [E07, E12, E23]

The hypothetical rescued bear case delivers approximately −21.92% annually, equivalent to roughly 71% terminal price loss from ₹80, even though cash is prefunded. The unrescued case has no defensible shareholder-return figure after a funding breach. Permanent-impairment risk is High because weak incremental returns, leverage and dilution can compound each other. It is not classified Severe on evidence of an actual default, since none was established. Recovery requires better capital turnover, durable collections, refinancing on reasonable terms and protection of minority claims. [E08, E13, E24]

The best counterargument is that existing capacity is already funded and underutilized, so higher throughput could generate revenue with much less future investment than the model assumes. The stronger rating and parent equity conversion support that view. The capex-turnover and deposit sensitivities test it, but a demonstrated improvement in adjusted operating cash and post-tax capital returns is needed before treating this counterargument as the base outcome. [E18, E23]

Implementation can magnify a loss. Of 60 scheduled exchange sessions through 19 October, 43 have issuer rows and 17 remain unresolved, not assumed zero-volume days. Across the 43 observed rows, mean traded value is ₹12.849 lakh and median ₹6.284 lakh; median volume is 10,000 shares. Only 16 of the latest 20 scheduled sessions have rows, with observed mean ₹21.0899 lakh and median ₹12.925 lakh. These are observed-sample statistics, not exact 20/60-day averages. The active SM lot is 2,000 shares, or ₹160,000 at the dated price; inactive SQ fields are stale and must not replace active-series terms. [E20]

For the ₹500,000 reference, continuous-value liquidation estimates at 2%, 5% and 10% of the lower observed mean/median are 39.78, 15.91 and 7.96 sessions. For three whole lots worth ₹480,000 they are 38.19, 15.28 and 7.64; four lots worth ₹640,000 give 50.92, 20.37 and 10.18. sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
paragraphs: A fivefold per-share gain in five years requires approximately 37.98% annualized; tenfold requires approximately 58.50%. Revenue growth alone is insufficient because shares may also expand and operating capital must be financed. At the base rescue share count of about 62.18 million, prices of ₹400 and ₹800 require equity values of about ₹2,487 crore and ₹4,974 crore. With base terminal debt and usable cash, those imply EV/EBITDA of roughly 53x and 107x on the modeled ₹46.80 crore terminal EBITDA. [E24]

These are arithmetic feasibility checks, not targets. They would require a substantially different combination of operating scale, margins, capital intensity, dilution and terminal valuation from the supported cases. No evidence-backed 5x/10x thesis is established. Optional defense, railway or overseas opportunities are not added as free terminal value.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
paragraphs: 1. Adjusted cash conversion: FY24–FY26 advance- and supplier-finance-neutral CFO after interest was negative ₹6.2654 crore. Require two comparable reporting periods of positive conversion without fresh parent advances before upgrading CASH. 2. Parent supplies/tooling advances: baseline ₹49.3715 crore at March 2026; monitor absolute growth, aging, application against shipments and repayment terms. A rapid fall without replacement liquidity is a funding warning. [E07, E09]

3. Parent-loan bridge: reconcile ₹14.7753 crore at March to ₹32 crore converted in October with dated receipts, reclassifications, interest and use of funds. 4. Deposits and restrictions: reconcile ₹4.8415 crore deposits, disclosed pledged amounts, Omnia cash and actual unencumbered balances. These two items determine whether the current funding hold can be lifted. 5. Receivable and inventory days: March 2026 closing ratios are about 60 and 80 sales-days; repeated movement above 75 and 95, respectively, calls for a cash-path refresh. [E13, E15, E28]

6. Incremental operating returns: gross three-year proxy is 4.52%; require improvement toward the 12%–16% capital-cost range, not merely a management ROCE headline. 7. Commissioning and Meeta economics: track ₹11.9421 crore CWIP, cash capex, monthly output and pretax profit; tax credits should not be mistaken for operating progress. 8. Audit logs and disclosure quality: seek documented database-level audit-trail operation and a reconciliation of the FY23 cash-flow anomaly. [E08, E10, E27, E29]

9. Dilution: reconcile all PECL and Meeta warrants separately, actual proceeds and expiry; never add subsidiary warrants to parent shares. 10. Implementation: refresh the official lot, active series, surveillance status, full 60-session tape and bid/ask depth before any trade. The ₹500,000 reference represents three whole lots at ₹480,000 or four at ₹640,000 at the dated quote, neither an assumed fill. [E16, E17, E20]

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
paragraphs: Classification: Hold: unresolved current funding and implementation evidence. Business quality is mixed/weak at BQS 4.9, growth quality is capped at 5.0, and investment attractiveness is NS. The company does not meet the compounder criteria because capital returns, cash realization, funding resilience and moat strength are below the required levels. The historical growth score is not an investment ranking. [E04, E08–E10, E24]

The appropriate action category is Research priority / unresolved watchlist, not an eligible buy or an instruction to sell an existing holding. The reader’s actual position, tax basis and constraints were not supplied. A lower price alone would not cure an incomplete funding bridge, lot-size constraints or ongoing dilution. Reassessment requires an authenticated cash/debt rollforward, sustainable financing and better incremental economics; then the same cash-linked valuation should be rerun rather than simply lowering the multiple or raising a qualitative score.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
paragraphs: The linked source register identifies primary annual reports, the SEBI prospectus, rating rationales, current exchange filings, the dated security master and the validated market sample. Evidence entries distinguish verified disclosures, calculations, management statements and analyst assumptions. Compact and full deliverables retain original numerical extracts, formulas, model rows and source hashes without reproducing copyrighted annual-report pages or personal allottee details.

Key unresolved questions are the cash origin and timing of the ₹17.2247 crore parent-loan increase; current unrestricted cash and facility availability; Meeta warrant holders, expiry and participation by PECL; current promoter encumbrances and executable depth; a fully reconciled FY23 consolidated cash-flow presentation; FY26 physical sales volumes; and actual completion economics of recent capital projects. They are not replaced by zeros or neutral factor scores.

All forecast assumptions are nominal INR assumptions. The 12%–16% capital-cost range, 25% tax, 15% equity hurdle, 7x–12x principal terminal multiples, 60/80/24 sales-day working-capital assumptions and rescue terms are analytical conventions rather than company guidance. Sensitivities and explicit failed solver brackets are part of the conclusion. An exact numerical reproduction verifies the calculations, not the truth of unobserved future financing.

name: Pritika Engineering Components Limited
summary:
Pritika Engineering Components is a capital-intensive castings and machining business serving tractor and commercial-vehicle supply chains, principally through its listed parent. It has scaled organically, but the evidence does not yet establish a self-financing compounder. Consolidated revenue grew at 25.28% annually from FY23 to FY26, while the incremental post-tax operating return on gross operating capital was only 4.52%. Customer advances from the parent explain much of the reported operating cash flow. [E04, E07, E08]

This is a cyclical capacity-expansion thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. At the dated ₹80 quotation, the actual post-allotment market capitalization is ₹260.52 crore. Ordinary prospective returns and a buy-price recommendation remain unscored because the March-to-October funding bridge is incomplete. A fully funded hypothetical rescue is costly: the base case requires ₹137.88 crore of net new equity over the modeled period and delivers approximately −1.89% annualized at ₹80. That is a scenario, not a prediction of an actual capital raise or evidence of a historical default. The decisive improvement would be collection-led cash generation and higher capacity returns without further parent-advance dependence. [E14, E15, E24]
